items: Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments report improved test-time selection across five domains — importance 5/10 · Guan and Du introduce Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments (APT), a training-free method that generates candidate solutions and selects a winner through single-elimination matchups. In each matchup, multiple prompted verifiers compare the two candidates along distinct aspects and vote; position-swapped judgments are used to reduce order bias. The authors report that APT produced the best score in 14 of 15 generator-domain pairs across five tasks and three generators at eight candidates, outperforming self-consistency, reward-model selection and binary aspect approval in most comparisons. Their matched-budget and component ablations also favor the combination of pairwise comparison and aspect-specific voting. These are preprint-reported results, not independent replications. The evaluation does not cover coding or long-form writing, and the tournament can cost up to about four times the input tokens of binary multi-aspect approval and adds sequential latency. — FCMO-E3444414CD0E

CLR-Bench tests whether self-evolving agents infer hidden rules from feedback — importance 4/10 · The 29 October arXiv preprint introduces CLR-Bench, a benchmark of 20 four-level curriculum chains across 10 constructed domains. It tests whether six self-evolution methods infer hidden named groupings from sparse feedback and transfer them to unseen values, rather than retaining corrections as exceptions. The authors report weak feedback-only generalization for GPT-6-Luna, improvement with a fixed lesson, and substantially stronger results for selected methods with GPT-6-Sol. These are author-reported results on a small constructed benchmark; they do not establish general agent learning or operational transfer. — FCMO-A2A624115206

OpenAI reports engineering-task gains and early industry workflows with AI models — importance 5/10 · In a 3 November 2026 report, OpenAI described engineering workflows and reported a 0.875 BenchCAD 2.0 result for a newer internal model versus 0.594 for GPT-6 Astra at maximum effort. BenchCAD’s current leaderboard now lists the unreleased OpenAI model on a separate, provider-credited Codex custom-harness board, using the 2.0 scorer and estimating cost at about $38 per case. BenchCAD says custom-harness and standard 2.1 scores are not comparable; the 0.875 remains an OpenAI-linked result without task-level run data or independent reproduction. BenchCAD 2.0 covers 100 held-out cases across CAD parts, assemblies and PCB connectivity, not manufacturability or physical performance. OpenAI also describes early engineer-reviewed work with Chip Ganassi Racing and Mazda, without measured productivity or production outcomes. — FCMO-260BC355EE27

Anthropic reports task-level patterns in scientists’ use of Claude — importance 5/10 · Anthropic’s 5 November 2026 report analyzes 207,049 consumer-plan Claude and Claude Code sessions classified as scientific work from 2 August to 30 September. It reports that data analysis and writing are common uses, while data gathering and ideation appear less often than their estimated share of researcher time. An LLM-based task-capability measure is associated with greater use: the top fifth of tasks receive about two to four times the use expected from researcher time. A separate survey of 528 active AI-using scientists broadly mirrors the task mix. These are first-party, classifier-based usage findings; the underlying conversations are not public for independent audit. The report does not measure research quality, causal productivity or realized scientific discoveries, and its future-output scenarios are hypothetical. Its 528-person survey recruited from Anthropic grant-program applicants in the US and Canada, likely a high-AI-use sample; the task-capability scores are also LLM-derived, so their relationship with product usage is not independent validation of capability. Its appendix tests the field/task classifier on 5,000 synthetic transcripts: reported accuracy is 69% for task and 58% for task-by-subfield, falling to 64% and 54% after excluding transcripts that retain label wording. High-confidence and high-contribution subsets preserve aggregate patterns, but the appendix says actual transcripts lack ground-truth task labels, so these checks do not independently establish real-session classification accuracy. — FCMO-7C052305DC76

China’s CAC launches a unified filing system for internet technology services — importance 4/10 · On 2026-11-09, China’s Cyberspace Administration said its new Internet New Technology and Application Information Service Filing System had entered operation. The notice says the system integrates filings for generative AI, algorithms, deep-synthesis services and blockchain, and that the former algorithm-filing and blockchain-service filing systems stopped operating. This records the regulator’s launch announcement; the portal opened without readable page text during this review, so actual workflows and filings were not independently inspected. — FCMO-A4EC3F3429ED
